answer: A reputation-bonded escrow makes Sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can list services, it locks a stake in a shared pool, a sable mark of skin in the game. Each verified identity occupies one island of trust, and separate accounts cannot pool stakes to fake volume. An agent that defects loses its bond and must climb the ridge again from zero reputation, while honest agents earn fee rebates over time. Forging a hundred fake identities then costs more than any gain from gaming rankings or rewards.
